p.src: 1  I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Friends Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved.

ja: 人たち 友人たちよ、
en: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Friends Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved.
u.src: 1  I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Friends Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved.

p.src: 2  I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It is the voice of my beloved who knocks: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night.”

ja: のしずくにぬれている。」
en: I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It is the voice of my beloved who knocks: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night.”
u.src: 2  I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It is the voice of my beloved who knocks: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night.”

p.src: 3  I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? I have washed my feet. Indeed, must I soil them?

en: I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? I have washed my feet. Indeed, must I soil them?
u.src: 3  I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? I have washed my feet. Indeed, must I soil them?

p.src: 4  My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening. My heart pounded for him.

ja: の胸はあの人を思って高鳴った。
en: My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening. My heart pounded for him.
u.src: 4  My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening. My heart pounded for him.

p.src: 5  I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock.

ja: けようと立ち上がった。
en: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock.
u.src: 5  I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock.

p.src: 6  I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left, and had gone away. My heart went out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t answer.

ja: っていた。 あの人が
の心は消え入るばかりだった。
en: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left, and had gone away. My heart went out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t answer.
u.src: 6  I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left, and had gone away. My heart went out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t answer.

p.src: 7  The watchmen who go about the city found me. They beat me. They bruised me. The keepers of the walls took my cloak away from me.

en: The watchmen who go about the city found me. They beat me. They bruised me. The keepers of the walls took my cloak away from me.
u.src: 7  The watchmen who go about the city found me. They beat me. They bruised me. The keepers of the walls took my cloak away from me.

p.src: 8  I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, that you tell him that I am faint with love.

ja: たちよ、あなたがたに誓わせる。
つけたなら、 私が恋い焦がれて弱っていると
en: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, that you tell him that I am faint with love.
u.src: 8  I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, that you tell him that I am faint with love.

p.src: 9  How is your beloved better than another beloved, you fairest among women? How is your beloved better than another beloved, that you do so adjure us?

ja: あなたの愛する人は、ほかの人よりどこがすぐれているのか。
は、ほかの人よりどこがすぐれているので、 私たちにそのように誓わせるのか。
en: How is your beloved better than another beloved, you fairest among women? How is your beloved better than another beloved, that you do so adjure us?
u.src: 9  How is your beloved better than another beloved, you fairest among women? How is your beloved better than another beloved, that you do so adjure us?

p.src: 10  My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among ten thousand.

en: My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among ten thousand.
u.src: 10  My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among ten thousand.

p.src: 11  His head is like the purest gold. His hair is bushy, black as a raven.

en: His head is like the purest gold. His hair is bushy, black as a raven.
u.src: 11  His head is like the purest gold. His hair is bushy, black as a raven.

p.src: 12  His eyes are like doves beside the water brooks, washed with milk, mounted like jewels.

ja: われ、宝石のように美しく
en: His eyes are like doves beside the water brooks, washed with milk, mounted like jewels.
u.src: 12  His eyes are like doves beside the water brooks, washed with milk, mounted like jewels.

p.src: 13  His cheeks are like a bed of spices with towers of perfumes. His lips are like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.

ja: 、香り草の小高い畝のよう。 その
en: His cheeks are like a bed of spices with towers of perfumes. His lips are like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.
u.src: 13  His cheeks are like a bed of spices with towers of perfumes. His lips are like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.

p.src: 14  His hands are like rings of gold set with beryl. His body is like ivory work overlaid with sapphires.

ja: は、サファイアを散りばめた
en: His hands are like rings of gold set with beryl. His body is like ivory work overlaid with sapphires.
u.src: 14  His hands are like rings of gold set with beryl. His body is like ivory work overlaid with sapphires.

p.src: 15  His legs are like pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

ja: はレバノンのよう、杉のようにひときわすぐれている。
en: His legs are like pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
u.src: 15  His legs are like pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

p.src: 16  His mouth is sweetness; yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.

ja: く、 そのすべてが慕わしい。 エルサレムの
en: His mouth is sweetness; yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.
u.src: 16  His mouth is sweetness; yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.
